componentPlan.focusQuote: Sequencing DNA means determining the order of the four chemical building blocks - called "bases" - that make up the DNA molecule.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks recall of core facts about sequencing and bases before deeper work

componentPlan.focusQuote: Adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T); cytosine (C) always pairs with guanine (G).
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Groups bases by pairing rules to reinforce complementary matching logic

overview.headline: DNA sequencing reads chemical bases to reveal genetic instructions and health clues

keyPoints.point: Sequencing DNA involves determining the order of chemical building blocks in the molecule
keyPoints.quote: Sequencing DNA means determining the order of the four chemical building blocks - called "bases" - that make up the DNA molecule.

keyPoints.point: Chemical bases bond with the same partner to form base pairs that copy when cells divide
keyPoints.quote: In the DNA double helix, the four chemical bases always bond with the same partner to form "base pairs."

keyPoints.point: The sequence tells scientists the kind of genetic information carried in a DNA segment
keyPoints.quote: The sequence tells scientists the kind of genetic information that is carried in a particular DNA segment.

keyPoints.point: Physicians use sequence data to identify the particular type of cancer for better treatment choices
keyPoints.quote: In cancer, for example, physicians are increasingly able to use sequence data to identify the particular type of cancer a patient has.

keyTerms.gloss: chemical building blocks that make up the DNA molecule
keyTerms.quote: Sequencing DNA means determining the order of the four chemical building blocks - called "bases" - that make up the DNA molecule.

keyTerms.gloss: pairing where chemical bases bond with the same partner to form units
keyTerms.quote: In the DNA double helix, the four chemical bases always bond with the same partner to form "base pairs."

keyTerms.gloss: instructions for making and maintaining a human being spelled in base pairs
keyTerms.quote: The human genome contains about 3 billion base pairs that spell out the instructions for making and maintaining a human being.

keyTerms.gloss: tiny pores used in new technology to sequence DNA strands
keyTerms.quote: Another new technology in development entails the use of nanopores to sequence DNA.

analysis.pageCoverage: Explains DNA sequencing definition, base pairing and copying, new polymerase and nanopore methods, and uses for health, disease and evolution research
analysis.subject: biology
